Read me.instruction: Compare published model configurations at their reported reasoning settings. Filter Results by model, benchmark, version, and effort.
Research retrieved September 6, 2026. This is a reproducible snapshot, not a live feed. Sources retain source dates when published.
Edit Results to change observations. Rerun the Python script. It reads this workbook into pandas and preserves it. Derived metrics and figures go into separate files.
cost_usd uses the unit in cost_basis. Coding and HLE costs are per attempt. AA Index uses a weighted task. ARC-AGI-3 uses the entire evaluation cost.
Most scores are percentages. AA Index is a composite index. FrontierCode is a weighted rubric score. ARC-AGI-3 measures action efficiency. Do not average these scales.
Effort labels are provider and benchmark settings, not interchangeable compute budgets. Source none can mean a default setting. Best observed means a maximum across settings, not max effort.
DeepSWE owner data omit Fable 5.1. Its vendor score 67.4% has no exact published cost. Terminal-Bench has only max for Sol and Fable 5.1. GLM-5.3 owner sweeps generally have only max.

DeepSWE uses expected Astra prices: $12/M input, $15/M cache write, $1.20/M cache read, $50/M output, and $2/M compute units. These differ from the direct API price sheet. Hollow plotted points flag this.
DeepSWE applies owner frontend price adjustments. Exact original costs and adjustment formulas are retained in Source records. Terminal-Bench and FrontierCode do not expose complete rate cards.
Use AA Intelligence Index v4.2 as one cohort. Lower-effort Fable, and some comparison models, have estimated index scores and missing suite costs. They are omitted from the index cost plot.
The main HLE panel uses AA text-only no-tools pass@1. Anthropic full-set no-tools and with-tools evaluations are separate rows. Their different graders, tools, and fallback policies affect scores.
AA HLE and GPQA costs include per-benchmark fallback token shares priced at Opus 4.8 rates. Source records retain the fractions, token counts, price rates, and formula.
Standard and Provider Adapter configurations remain separate. Astra none research variants are preserved in Results but omitted from the main plot because its public API does not support none.

DeepSWE intervals are 95% run-to-run intervals over four passes. Terminal-Bench owner intervals retain the reported 95% bounds. Small point-estimate differences do not establish statistical significance.

The derived workbook marks Pareto efficiency within one benchmark, version, cost unit, and harness. Provisional, estimated, or known outdated price comparisons are excluded. A Pareto point has no cheaper equally good or better eligible observation. Astra research variants without published API support are excluded.

For binary success metrics, usd_per_success = mean attempt cost / (score / 100). This aggregate includes failed attempts and does not assume retries are independent. No such metric is computed for partial-credit scores or indexes.
Prices are USD per million tokens and record context tiers, cache rates, and promotions. They are not task-cost estimates. Long sessions, paid tools, hosting, and discounts can change your own bill.
The standalone script embeds this entire dataset as compressed JSON. Dependencies are in its Python script metadata. Installed dependencies suffice to regenerate all artifacts offline.
678 observations, 43 exact model labels, 89 source links. Comparison and historical rows remain identifiable.
